# pages/api/ — server-side proxy routes (the ONLY backend)

*Generated by index-knowledge · commit 917d399 · branch main. See ../../AGENTS.md for project-wide conventions.*

## OVERVIEW
Three Next.js Pages-Router handlers that proxy third-party APIs the browser can't call directly (CORS, secret signing, or HA-internal). Everything else in the app is client-side.

## WHERE TO LOOK
| Route | Purpose | Notes |
|-------|---------|-------|
| `awn.ts` | Ambient Weather Network device list | Incoming params are `awn`-prefixed; the `ambient-weather-api` lib wants `apiKey`/`applicationKey` — the rename is intentional. Returns raw `Device[]`; client uses `[0]`. |
| `ha/sun2.ts` | Discover HA Sun2 sunrise/sunset sensor pairs | Needs `SUPERVISOR_TOKEN` (HA add-on only) → otherwise 503 and the client falls back to the provider's sun. Pairs sensors by `_sun_rising`/`_sun_setting` suffix. |
| `switchbot.ts` | SwitchBot device status | HMAC-SHA256 signed (`token`+`t`+`nonce`). |

## ANTI-PATTERNS / GOTCHAS
- **`switchbot.ts` hardcodes a device id (`ED505FE38F0D`) and `zipcode:'80465'`** — personal/experimental, not generalized and not wired into the main UI flow. Do NOT treat it as a template.
- `awn.ts` does no error handling — an upstream throw becomes a 500; the client treats 401 as bad credentials.
- No auth on any route. Under the add-on's direct port 8099 they're LAN-exposed (documented trade-off in `homeassistant/config.yaml`).
- Runs under `next start` inside the add-on; nginx rewrites `/api/` with the ingress prefix (`homeassistant/nginx.conf`).
